chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Sulayman ibn Hilal, who said:

One of our companions asked Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام and said: May I be your ransom, a man sleeps with another man under one cover? He said: “Are they of unmarriageable kin?” He said: No. He said: “Out of necessity?” He said: No. He said: “They are to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.”

He said: And if he did it? He said: “If it was short of penetration, then the hadd; and if he penetrated, he is to be stood upright and then struck one blow with the sword—the sword takes from him whatever it takes.” He said: So I said to him: Then that is killing? He said: “That is so.”

I said: And a woman who sleeps with a woman under one cover? He said: “Are they of unmarriageable kin?” I said: No. He said: “Out of necessity?” I said: No. He said: “They are to be struck with thirty lashes, thirty lashes.” I said: And if she did it? He said: That weighed heavily upon him, so he said: “Uff, uff, uff,” three times, and he said: “The hadd.”

key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a person within prohibited degrees of marriage due to kinship
key_terms.سَوْطًا: a lash or stroke used in corporal punishment
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: a state of necessity that may affect the legal ruling
key_terms.لِحَافٍ: one shared cover or blanket under which two people sleep

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhib al-Ahkam on two men or two women sleeping under one cover and on same-sex sexual acts?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام concerning two men or two women sleeping together under one cover without kinship or necessity, and the punishments associated with that conduct. It further distinguishes between lesser sexual misconduct and penetration, assigning hadd punishments accordingly, and thus belongs to the jurisprudential discussions of criminal law and sexual prohibitions.
